utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I put on the record that Mr. Mladic is not attending today. Yesterday he explicitly waived his right to be present, and counsel, Mr. Lukic, is in court. The second issue I'd like to put on the record is that Judge Moloto is, for urgent reasons, unable to sit today. This will be of limited duration. It's only for today, not any longer, and Judge Fluegge and myself have decided that it's in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case under Rule 15 bis. Then the Prosecution announced that it would wish to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. And a very brief matter. As the Chamber is aware, Mr. Theunens is stationed in Lebanon at the moment and involved in a security-related position. There have been evolving events in Lebanon this week. The Prosecution is requesting that the Chamber instruct VWU just to request or -- inquire from Mr. Theunens whether there's any problem and how long is he able to stay and whether there's any -- because we are unaware of his present position. And secondly, Your Honour, next week we're not scheduled to sit Wednesday. If the Chamber would also consider if -- whatever the situation, if there is one with Mr. Theunens, if sitting Wednesday instead of Friday would facilitate his return, if that's necessary, that the Chamber would consider that. The Defence -- I discussed it with the Defence and they have no objection for that change in schedule. And we would appreciate the Chamber's consideration. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will certainly consider it. At the same time, the parties should be aware that since we're sitting four days a week, the Judges started filling their agendas on Wednesday quite heavily, and we'll have to see whether that still can be changed. But we'll consider it. Much may also depend on any commitment of the Defence on finishing cross-examination within the time estimates. Then could Mr. Theunens be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, Mr. Weber, I make the following observation. The Chamber urged you very much to seek to introduce documentary evidence through the witness because the Chamber was concerned about the 434 documents still to be bar tabled. The Chamber counted the new documents, documents not yet in evidence which were introduced through Mr. Theunens, and I think we are at a total of five, which is a relatively low number. I leave it to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a difference in counting. Other counts say it's ten, Mr. Weber. But whether it's five or whether it's ten, apparently you ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When I said "five," I meant to say five that were on the bar table motion, which now moved to viva voce introduction. That number is relatively low, and the Chamber just hopes that you're not relying on that when you don't move them in through the witness, that they'll automatically be admitted from the bar table. Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apologies for continuing with other matters when you entered the courtroom. Perhaps needless to say, but you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave and Mr. Weber will now continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P474, page 3 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we left off discussing the 6th of June. Coming up before you will be operational directive number one issued by General Mladic on 6 June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could I please have page 3 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on this page, it indicates there are two stages planned for VRS operations pursuant to Directive 1. Could you please assist us with letting us know what part of the overall strategy as defined by the six strategic objectives are being implemented by General Mladic in this part of the directive?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the first stage describes, it talks about operations in the -- around Sarajevo airport, as well as deblocking communications on the Sarajevo-Trnovo road, Trnovo being controlled by the Bosnian Serb. So this can be seen in the context of strategic goal number five, maintaining the division of Sarajevo. And secondly, mention is also made of the grouping of forces to open the corridor between Semberija and Bosnian Krajina which corresponds with strategic goal number 2. Of course, I mean, when you look at these directives and subsequent orders and the manner in which these orders are implemented -- I mean, the directives and orders are implemented, they also result in the implementation of strategic goal number 1; i.e., the separation of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday at the end of the day we looked at an entry General Mladic's notes on the same day of this directive. Does directive 1 reflect the areas and objectives discussed during General Mladic's meeting with the other Bosnian Serb leaders?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour, and I refer to my comment about the wider vicinity of Sarajevo airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page of directive 1, we see the tasks for the East Bosnia Corps or IBK, the SRK, and the Herzegovina Corps. First focusing on the IBK, General Mladic instructs this corps to secure the Zvornik-Milici-Vlasenica road and mop up or cleanse Birac of the remaining enemy forces. With respect to this reference to Birac, is this the same area near Zvornik where we saw the 28 May 1992 order from the Birac Brigade to the Zvornik TO yesterday, the order that said move out the women and children and place them into camps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the next paragraph are the tasks for the SRK. General Mladic orders the SRK to regroup in such a way to mop up or cleanse parts of Sarajevo with a majority Serb population. He then goes on to specify a number of particular areas. Have you reviewed orders carrying out these operations as part of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I did, Your Honour, and -- and, you know, maintaining not only Serb control over parts of Sarajevo that had a Serbian majority or a significant Serb presence as well as ensuring the implementation of strategic goal number 5, the division of Sarajevo is an operation -- is a goal that is pursued throughout the 1992 to 1995 conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P458.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a set of instructions dated 7 June 1992, a day after the directive. They're from SRK corps commander Tomislav Sipcic to subordinate commands of the SRK. Do these instructions show that Directive 1 was immediately implemented by the SRK Command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we should we would have to go to the page that shows the decision of the commander of the SRK and the orders he gives to his subordinate brigade commanders. But I mean, I remember this document, and the answer is affirmative to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 11468. For the record, a copy of this document is referenced in Mr. Theunens's report under 65 ter 16989. The Prosecution is using this copy since it has been referenced previously during these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a report from SRK corps Commander Sipcic to the Main Staff dated 17 June 1992 concerning the status of combat operations. Could you please tell us whether this report shows that the SRK carried out Directive 1.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it shows that. And just referring back to what we discussed earlier, the two-down principle, here you can see that the corps commander reports to the Main Staff about the activities of the brigade; i.e., two down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, directing your attention to paragraphs 6 and 7 of this document, do you have any comments on these paragraphs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, paragraph 6 discusses -- I mean, quote/unquote, treatment of civilian population where a distinction is made between Serbs and non-Serbs in a sense that Croats are left together with the Serbs, but Muslims are being separated from them. And this, I mean this corresponds with the first strategic goal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 11468 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to the document. We do believe that the witness has misrepresented it, but no objection to the document itself coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives number P3059, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3059 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, probably for the remainder of this session I want to go to a couple of other topics and then I will return to the directives. On page 242 of Part 2 of your report, you concluded that General Mladic was: "... in constant contact with his subordinate units, including by being present at forward command posts near the zone of operations where VRS units conduct significant combat operations." Generally could you tell us how General Mladic's presence in the field at these forward command posts facilitated his ability to exercise command and control over VRS units.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, summarising the documents I have reviewed in that context, and these can be found in footnotes 924, 925 -- actually it should be 925, I'm sorry, of Part 2 of the report. By being present as close as possible to the area where the fighting is conducted, communication lines are shortened, it's easier, for example, for General Mladic to be in direct contact, direct physical contact with subordinate commanders. He may well be visible there by the soldiers which given the personality of General Mladic can be considered a motivating factor. I base this conclusion again on reports of subordinate commanders after visits conducted by General Mladic to his subordinated units. So the shortened communication lines allow it is for General Mladic to be better informed and also to interact more closely with the subordinate commanders who -- of the units that are conducting the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 09859.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to go through a few documents with you related to General Mladic's presence in the field. This is a 1st Krajina Corps information report from General Talic dated 17 July 1992. How does this report demonstrate General Mladic's presence in the field?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document shows that General Mladic, together with, as it is identified in the document, the corps members of the 1 KK command visits the forward defence lines of the 1st KK that are involved in Operation Corridor; i.e., to establish the corridor between Semberija or strategic goal number 2. General Mladic congratulates soldiers, and, I mean, he's in direct interaction with them, and he also inspects actually or he observes himself the level of implementation of the corps that have been set, and this we can connect then to the directive we discussed this morning, Directive number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 9859. The Prosecution also notes just for the record that operational directive 1 provides orders to OG Doboj and the same operational group is also mention in the directive number 3 which we'll discuss later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to the introduction of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3060, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3060 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 21 January 1994 order from General Mladic to the SRK Command. What does the first paragraph above the word "order" indicate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I can see the bottom of the document in the B/C/S version. It shows that General Mladic has to the -- that part of the -- of the Sarajevo front. It's not always easy to read the English, I must say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It should be enlarged in such a way that the witness can read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because also in the previous document, I mean, I can try to put my head on the monitor but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to provide you with legible texts. Could we enlarge a little bit more the English. Is this sufficient, Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or would you still need it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honours. Thank you. Yes, I just wanted to see who signed it, but I could see that also on the B/C/S version, but it shows that General Mladic, going back again to the first paragraph of the order, that he has toured the Sarajevo front, I mean, or section of the Sarajevo front, and based on that issues additional orders to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 6 that we see before us, General Mladic orders that he is to be kept informed of the execution of these preparations.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How does this relate to his order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As was discussed during the previous days, this is a regular procedure for a commander to, yeah, confirm that the subordinate commanders have to report on the degree of implementation or the status of implementation of orders. And just very briefly, when you look at the order -- I mean, General Mladic, looking at paragraphs 3, 4, 5, he gives orders which are actually, I would say, instructions of a very tactical nature where you would almost expect a battalion commander to take care of these kind of issues. So to me, and I have also illustrated that in the report with other examples, it highlights how closely General Mladic is monitoring the way how his subordinate commanders implement his -- his orders. And again, yeah, gives very detailed instructions of almost a tactical nature which should be way below his level of responsibility as commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 50 into evidence and further notes that this order is one day before Scheduled Incident G6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't object to the document. But are we now making submissions about the documents or are we just entering evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Sometimes it is a short way, if you want to deal with a document and where the one says date A and the other date A plus 1, then it can be a short and efficient way, unless there's any specific reason why you should doubt as to whether the dates are accurate, yes or no. Of course, you could ask the same question, is this -- but Mr. Weber, there's no specific need to do that. Dates are dates. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P3061, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3 -- P3061 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1028.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before you is the 2 March 1993 order from General Mladic to conduct a tour of inspection of the Drina Corps units. If we could focus on paragraph 1 which continues at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can that be enlarged further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This paragraph continues onto the next page. When was this inspection to occur and for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the document states the inspection is to occur from 3 to 4 March 1993, and the purpose is to assess the combat readiness of four brigades of the Drina Corps, which, again, is -- is an application of the two-down principle. What is of interest is that the inspection team is to be - I think that's further visible in the document - is to be led by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please see the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh. I mean, I stand corrected because I see that -- I must be confused with another document, I'm sorry, because paragraph 2 -- paragraph 2 highlights or explains who are the members. So I'm sorry, I can find it in another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to this document, does it show that other members of the VRS Main Staff were also carrying out the inspection function of command and control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and that is consistent with the role of the staff because the staff is to assist the commander, so the commander cannot do everything himself obviously, and he can delegate certain tasks. And obviously for such a task, it would make sense indeed to delegate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We'll come back later to the operations that were going on at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, though, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 1028 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives number P3062, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3062 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1018.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a report from Radislav Krstic at the time of the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade Command to the Command of the Drina Corps, six days later. If we could please turn to page 2 of the English; specifically item 4. We see that Krstic is reporting that: "During the day, our brigade was visited by members of the General Staff headed by General Ratko Mladic." How does this visit relate to General Mladic's carrying out of an inspection?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you read the rest of the paragraph, Your Honours, paragraph 4, it explicitly states that the members of the Main Staff headed by General Mladic inspected our, i.e., the units of the 2nd Romanija Brigade, their positions, and also familiarised themselves with the situation on the front line and the conditions in which combat operations are conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 1018 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P3063, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 13 June 1994 order from General Mladic. As we can see, it was sent to all corps. If we could scroll down, and if you could please further describe to us what the purpose of this order is.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I discuss this document in footnote 1289 of the second part of my report, page 349. It concerns inspection visit -- or field inspection basically conducted between 16th of June to the 2nd of July 1994. And the team is being led by Lieutenant-Colonel General Mladic, and the purpose of the visit -- I mean, I cannot see that on this part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the next page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I'm reading from my report now. Yes, in -- under the section "I order," so paragraphs 1, you see what the task of the inspection team are. And it -- okay, they have to look in the combat readiness situation of commands and units, the levels of preparedness, the implementation of tasks contained in Directives in 1 to 6. So it shows that subsequent direction -- directive is not necessarily placed in all directives. I mean the strategic goals, the six strategic goals do not change during the conflict, so if the goal set then or task set in a directive have not been fully accomplished, they can be reiterated in a new directive. Yeah. And then there are, I would say, less important aspects to verify the preparation for Vidovdan Day, which corresponds with the 28th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 69 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives P3064, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P731.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before you will be a 11 April 1994 order for further action from Visegrad TG commander Dragisa Masal. We can see that this was sent to the 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 5th Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade and the Visegrad TG command post. If we could scroll down to the bottom of the English, we see under item 7 the document forwards a message from General Mladic who visited the area on 10 April. It indicates that General Mladic's message was: "Keep pushing energetically onwards. Pay no attention to what is going on around us. The Turks must disappear from these areas." What does this message show?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the message shows that General Mladic was in the area around that time, so on the 10th of April, and he gives actually an oral order, which the commander of the tactical group considers sufficiently important to cite it in his order to his subordinate units, and the text is visible. I mean, there were no Turkish troops. I understand that the word "Turks" is used for the Muslims or Bosniaks, and it's often considered a derogatory term for the Muslim nationality, which later called themselves Bosniaks in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 430.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 1 March 1995 order from General Mladic. Could you please tell us what this order relates to.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, this order relates to the situation in the Trnovo sector. And it -- I mean, when you look further on in the order, it refers to a meeting between the SRK, Herzegovina Corps Command, as well as representatives of the VRS Main Staff and the RS MUP in the context of conducting operations in the general sector of Trnovo because there's an important communication line for the Bosnian Serbs in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And under item 1, what does General Mladic order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He orders to create a so-called combat team consisting of -- of military and police personnel, obviously in order to facilitate command and control over VRS and RS MUP units conducting operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And is that area the area of Trnovo and Treskavica?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We see at the very beginning it says "at the SRK IKM," what does this show about the presence of the SRK in this area of Trnovo and Treskavica?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it shows that the SRK has established a forward command post there to facilitate command and control over forces operating in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 430 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives number P3065, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P1509. If we can please zoom in on the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 12 July 1995 dispatch from Dragomir Vasic of the Zvornik CJB. What does this document show that General Mladic was doing during his time in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document in the second paragraph shows that General Mladic holds a meeting or attends a meeting at the Bratunac Brigade command at 8.00 in the morning on the 12th of July. This meeting is also attended by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you have any other comments on this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I discuss this document in my report, and I'm trying to locate where it is in order to see if I have additional comments. At least it shows that General Mladic is in Bratunac on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll move on. For reference, it's in Part 2 footnote 1303.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's okay, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, the paragraph -- the last sentence of paragraph 5 is also quite indicative about the -- "What is to do be done with the civilian population?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 333 to 352 of Part 2 of your report, you discuss the situational awareness of General Mladic as the commander of the VRS. Could you please, first, define the concept of situational awareness.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I took the following definition for situational awareness. The understanding of the operational environment in the context of a commander's task. This is a definition I took from a doctrinal document from the United Kingdom Ministry of Defence. I have not been able to find the concept of situational awareness as such in SFRY armed forces doctrine, but what we have been discussing over the past two days, the two-down principle corresponds with the same; that is, that a commander has to be familiar with the activities of his units two levels down, not just confined to the units but also all other aspects that can influence the conduct of operations like, I mean, that's what we call the operational environment, the weather, the enemy forces, logistical constraints, and so on and so on. So all these factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on your analysis, what can you conclude as to the level of situational awareness possessed by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my conclusion is that General Mladic has a very high level of situational awareness, and this is, for example, visible through the inspections and other visits he conducts as well as meetings with subordinate commanders. It is also visible through the regular combat reports that are submitted to him. And as we have also seen over the past days, if he feels that he is not adequately informed he -- he himself or a subordinate member of the Main Staff contacts the unit for which he believes, I mean General Mladic believes, that he is not adequately informed and issues additional instructions in order to rectify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I would now like to discuss with you the military justice system in the VRS. There are three sections of your report where you discuss the topic of military justice and military discipline and the application of the Law of Armed Conflict. They are in Part 1 of your report on pages 88 to 112 and Part 2 of your report on pages 90 to 103, and pages 322 to 333. Could you please briefly tell us how these three sections of your report relate to one another?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first section, i.e., pages 88 to 112 of Part 1, discuss the legal and doctrinal framework as it existed for the SFRY armed forces, and most importantly there in addition, obviously, to the All People's Defence law, we have the 1988 regulation on the application of international laws of war in the armed forces of SFRY. It is my conclusion that these were still valid in the 1992 to 1995 time-period, including for the VRS. In the second section, I discuss the VRS military discipline system and military justice system, which is based on the military discipline and justice system that existed in the JNA and the SFRY armed forces, and we see that various laws and -- and regulations are adopted and also guide-lines are issued. And then in the last section, I discuss how this system is implemented during the 1992 to 1995 war, reviewing orders issued by General Mladic -- I should start first by Mr. Karadzic, General Mladic, as well as other members of the Main Staff in order to enforce military discipline in the armed forces. There are also examples included of investigations ordered by General Mladic. And -- and -- and, yeah, related documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Going to the 1988 regulations and the parts that you discuss on pages 93 and 94 of Part 1, what do these express in terms of the commander's legal responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, they show, first of all, that a commander is responsible for the action of his subordinates, and this can be found in paragraph 21 of the 1988 regulations. It also shows that an officer has to report violations of the laws of war if he has learned that such violations may have taken place. Paragraph 22 of the 1988 regulations discusses the responsibility for violations of the laws of war committed on orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's okay with you, at this time the Prosecution would simply tender the 1988 regulations. They've been uploaded under 65 ter 4377A. An exhibit number has been reserved for these regulations as P2185, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the -- how many pages are we dealing with? And how relevant are all of these pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We've gone through it and looked at in light of a number of witnesses that have commented on it. We've reduced multiple chapters, but we've included all the relevant chapters, and I think it is approximately -- I can check. I believe it's over 50 pages, but they're all relevant pages, in the Prosecution's view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it has a -- a number has already been reserved. P2185 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, it is -- we're one minute short from the usual time where we take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Whenever it's good for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could already Mr. Theunens be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, at the same time, our conversation yesterday at the end of the session was about timing. I expressed some views; you expressed some views. Anything new to be reported?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to finish today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that report. We take a break. We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 323 to 325 of Part 2, you discuss orders from General Mladic instructing that perpetrators of certain particular acts be prosecuted or subjected to disciplinary measures. What conclusions do you draw from these orders?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I conclude from these orders that General Mladic has the authority to order investigations and -- but he uses this authority only I would say selectively; i.e., the focus of the enforcement of the military discipline and justice system, including his powers to order investigations, are focussed on violations or crimes that are directly related to the manner in which subordinates conduct operations; i.e., if General Mladic sees certain shortcomings in the manner they were conducted, he orders an investigation. I have not seen any documents by General Mladic or -- or the Main Staff for the investigation of alleged violations of the laws of war conducted by members of the VRS or other units operating under the command of the Main Staff. There are certain documents, not specifically for General Mladic, but for the RS and VRS in general concerning the investigation of alleged violations of the laws of war, but those are focused on alleged violations committed by members of the opponents' forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 647.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before you will be a 17 August 1992 order from General Mladic. And could you please explain to us what this order shows in relation to what you just told us.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this -- this is in my view one of the examples that illustrates or that forms the basis for my conclusion, that is, that General Mladic, in this order, highlights a number of what he calls negative acts, and with negative acts he means activities that have a negative impact on combat readiness and the ability of the armed forces to conduct combat operations. I mean, from the title you can see there is a focus on -- on desertions, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, it says: "Defecting to the enemy or wilfully deserting a combat position by members of the RS army are to be energetically prevented by all means, including the use of weapons." What do you make of this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the text is -- is clear. I haven't seen any -- any combat report or -- or other report indicating that, indeed, weapons were used to prevent people or members of the VRS from deserting. There is information, but again I haven't found a document about that, but, for example, situation in September 1995 in the wider Sanski Most area that there Arkan and his volunteers are present, among other things, to prevent members of the VRS from abandoning combat positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 647 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document receives number P3066, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3066 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 14522.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This will be a 1 November 1994 order from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we enlarge the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we can please scroll down to the lower portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what this example demonstrates?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another example, Your Honour, of General Mladic using his authority to order investigations. In the specific case of members of the VRS, and here he refers to -- to commanding officers, of personnel, who wilfully retreat or abandon defence positions. And this document has to be seen in the context of the situation in -- in the western part of Bosnia-Herzegovina around that time, where we have a major offensive of the 5th ABiH Corps from Bihac in eastern direction forcing the VRS to retreat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 14522 into evidence. The Prosecution does have seven more examples that it would like to go through. At this time, we're happy to tendered these also from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And to the suggestion by Mr. Weber that he would tender the other ones as demonstrative of the same? Does Mr. Ivetic know what numbers they are --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, could you -- of course, we couldn't expect Mr. Ivetic to express himself on documents not known to him. For this one, Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P3067, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence. I take it then, Mr. Weber, that you have seven more examples of where General Mladic orders that, in case of certain violations, that investigation and criminal charges should follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's on the same topic, where -- yes. I mean, there -- they're not all necessarily from General Mladic but they relate to the same manner of senior members and what types of disciplinary measures were taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I suggest that you sit together with Mr. Ivetic - coffee or tea, I leave that to you - and see whether there's any objection against them to be admitted. If there is agreement, perhaps you could provide the 65 ter numbers already in advance to Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At page 102 of Part 2, you discuss reports on the work of the military prosecutor offices and what kinds of charges are reflected there. I have two questions in this respect. First, can you conclude whether or not the charges reflected in those documents are consistent with the priorities shown by General Mladic's orders we have just seen, to enforce military discipline?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed Your Honours. I mean, most of -- or the cases that are dealt with by the military prosecutors all refer to violations and breaches of military discipline and military justice that directly affect or that are directly related to combat activities. I have not seen any reports of cases concerning alleged violations of the laws of war by members of the VRS in these reports of the prosecutor's offices as well the VRS military courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have P1963, page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we're going to be returning to a discussion of the directives. Before you is operational directive number 3 from General Mladic dated 3 August 1992. I would like to draw your attention to section 2 of this directive, which states: "In operations to date, the SR BH army has achieved significant results in protecting the Serbian people and their centuries-old home. "Safe corridors have been established and the Serbian territories linked, while large losses and manpower and MTS have been inflicted on the enemy." Do you have any comments on this first part and what is its purpose of this retrospective recap in a directive, more generally.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, directives, they start with an overview of the current situation including the alleged activities of -- of enemy forces. The reference to protecting the Serbian people and their centuries-old home is, I think, is a constant between even end of 1991, but for sure when the VRS starts in various documents of the -- starts with -- is established, sorry. In various documents from the VRS Main Staff and subordinate commands that basically the Bosnian Serbs are fighting or have been forced to fight a war, which is in their view a defensive war, that is intended at protecting the Serbian population and defending Serbian lands, quote/unquote. And this was expressed in the first sentence of title 2. The reference to the safe corridors corresponds with the establishment of the so-called Posavina corridor between Krajina and Semberija, i.e., strategic goal number 2, as well as also strategic goal number 3, establishment of a corridor in the Drina valley and eliminating the Drina as a border, even if strategic goal number 3 is not fully realised at the stage of the release of Directive number 3 on the 3rd of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to the remainder of this section, do you have any comments on this directive and what the tasks are ordering at the operational/tactical level?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we would have to see the section with the tasks, but in my report on page 110, English version, second part, I discuss which goals Directive number 3 foresees to implement. We spoke about strategic goal number 2. There are reference to strategic goal number 5, as well as to strategic goals -- strategic goal number -- number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we just quickly go to the next page in the English and page 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could please scroll down just a little bit further about -- under operation objectives.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please just go through which parts refer to those specific strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Preventing the breaking of the blockade of Sarajevo, Your Honours, corresponds with strategic goal number 5; i.e., maintaining the blockade of -- maintaining the division, I'm sorry, of Sarajevo. Determinedly defend axes leading from Cazin Krajina and western Herzegovina towards central Bosnia, as well as Dubrovacka Zupa towards Herzegovina is -- is -- I mean, is a mixture of the various objectives because they are parts of objective number 2, corridor; number three, elimination of the Drina as a border; number 4 to set the borders of the -- the RS on the Una and Neretva river. Then we have another reference to Sarajevo. The fourth bullet, I mean, crushing the, quote/unquote, Ustasha forces in Posavina and Majevica, this corresponds with goal number 2, the corridor. Then below that we see the reference to Neretva. And -- and I mean, explicit reference to border areas of Serbian territories which is strategic goal number 4. Some reference to strategic goal number 3 when you look at Gorazde. And I believe further on -- I mean, I thought there was also reference to the access to the sea in the document, but that's maybe further on in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the first one you read, only prevent the breaking of the blockade of Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it continue -- links that to strategic goal number 5. It continues: And also prevent the penetration of Ustasha forces from Croatia and Central Bosnia towards the corridors in Posavina. Would that be -- could we link that to strategic goal number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina, could that be in relation to the strategic goal preventing the Drina river to be the border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, number 3. And there's also a reference -- what can be seen in the context of number 4, establishing a border on the Neretva because Herzegovina we're talking about -- I mean, this is the wider area of the Neretva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we move onto another document. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 02459.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the 21st Presidency Session held on 2 August 1992, a day before the issuance of Directive 3. The session was attended by Ratko Mladic, Radovan Karadzic, Koljevic, Plavsic, Krajisnik, and Colonel Tolimir. The agenda for the meeting includes under item 2 an assessment of the military situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Under item 2, we see that Mladic briefed those present on the military situation, describing the situation in each combat sector, necessary tasks, and other matters. It is noted in these minutes that: "Due to security considerations and the detailed nature of the information, the conclusions and alternatives adopted were not put on the record." Based on these minutes and your review of materials from other sessions where General Mladic was present, what observations do you have about General Mladic's role at either assembly sessions or in these Presidency meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object. The witness has been tendered as a military analyst expert. Now he's being asked to opine as to political and historical matters which goes the scope of his stated expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The mere fact that matters are considered, including some historical aspects, doesn't mean that the subject matter is outside the scope of the expertise of the witness. You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you need me to repeat the yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I can answer it. On English page 334 of the second part of the report, I provide an overview of meetings of the Supreme Command and/or the Presidency which are attended by General Mladic or other senior representatives of the VRS Main Staff throughout May 1992 to November 1995 time-period. And from those we can conclude that General Mladic is the -- yeah, the main interlocutor for the Supreme Command and the Presidency to be informed about the military situation in -- in -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Footnote 1221, for example, even if -- refers to a decision of the Presidency to establish a procedure whereby General Mladic can keep them informed on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 2459 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number P3068, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3068 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And just for the clarification of transcript, 65 ter number is 2549.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You misspoke, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And thank you. Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P3033.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just continuing on the same topic, coming up before you will be the minutes of the 21st Session of the SRBiH Presidency. We can see from the document who's present. At the bottom of the page, it indicates that General Mladic and General Gvero arrive during the session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please have the next page of the English version and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Again, we see that the generals brief the Presidency in detail on military and strategic questions and other matters, and there's also a similar language about the matters not being put on the record. Do these minutes show that the Bosnian Serb political leadership, including Karadzic and Krajisnik, were receiving detailed briefings from General Mladic during the course of operations that were being carried out pursuant to Directive 3?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do, Your Honours. And, again, as I mentioned earlier, it's not restricted to a specific directive. It's throughout the May 1992 to November 1995 time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 689.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We have looked at a couple of Presidency minutes that indicate the Bosnian Serb political leadership were briefed in detail about military strategic matters related to the VRS at their meetings. I want to now turn your attention to the Bosnian Serb political leadership's presence at military meetings. This is a document dated 7 November 1992 from General Manojlo Milovanovic to the VRS corps and the Doboj OG commander. What does this document relate to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document has to be seen in context with the corridor 92 operation. I would call it a second series of corridor 92 operations to establish a corridor between Semberija and Serbia actually and Bosanska Krajina and also the Croatian Krajina, i.e., strategic goal number 2, and such operations were conducted, first, in June/July 1992, and the second series of operations of the same type were conducted in November 1992, and those are discussed paged 198 and following in Part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this -- this order from -- this order that's mentioned in Part 1, what time and place is this meeting supposed to occur?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the document states, Your Honour, a meeting is called for the 8th of November, 1992, in Bijeljina barracks, with the member -- with General Mladic's as well as the members of the Presidency, the corps commanders, the commander of the -- the air force and defence forces, and the commander of OG Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tender this is document at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P3069, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P356, page 141 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Coming up before you will be an 8th November 1992 entry from General Mladic's notebooks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These two versions seem to be -- not to correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to move quicker to -- to focus on some specific points, I'll just briefly indicate for the record that we see that it's a meeting on Sunday, the 8th of November, 1992, between 10.37 and 5.00. As we can see from this first page, Radovan Karadzic is present, and on this page - and if we could just go forward in the following pages eventually to page 145 - we can see that the various corps commanders give reports and also the commander of the Doboj operations group, Colonel Simic? After this, we see that General Mladic's notes indicate he discussed the strategic and operational position of the army of the RS and assignments for further actions. Karadzic then, according to these notes, offers congratulations and states: "The army and our courageous officers contributed enormously to the results we have achieved to date." If we could go on to the next page of both versions, we see that Mr. Karadzic is recorded as at the end of his comments as stating: "Maybe it would be good" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down while reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the end, Karadzic states: "Maybe it would be good if we solved the issue of the Drina." Based on the notes of this meeting so far, and in relation to the document that we just looked at, is this the meeting that was discussed in that previous document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the absence of information concerning another meeting and taking into account the duration of this meeting, which covers the largest part of the day, I think that's a reasonable conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this page and next, General Mladic records Krajisnik speaking and offering his admiration of the military. He then states: "We have a disproportionate engagement of the army in relation to the strategic objectives." Could we please have the next page. He then indicates: "We have not achieved: The Neretva; the sea; the Podrinje area." And he states what: "We have achieved: The corridor; separation with Muslims." As of November 1992, does this assessment accurately reflect the achieved and non-achieved objectives from the Bosnian Serb six strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Krajisnik continues to state: "We must bring the war to an end. The most pressing thing is to mop up Orasje and then to solve the problem of the Podrinje area and the Neretva river valley as soon as possible ..." He then states: "The Muslims must not stay with us and they should not be given any kind of autonomy. "The most important objective is the task assigned to Zivanovic - the mopping up the Drina - the most important task is separation from the Muslims." What is Krajisnik referring to in this part of these -- these notes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean which strategic goals or?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, if could you first indicate what it is he saying in relation to the strategic goals, but then secondly if could you comment on the task that he's discussing with respect to Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object. Now the witness is being asked to opine about what a politician is talking about as to a strategic objective. Again, this witness has been presented as a purported military analyst expert, meaning that he is related -- in relation to the command and control within the military, so I don't think that offering speculation or opinion as to what politicians mean by their words is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since this politician is engaged in a meeting with the military, it's relevant. At the same time, Mr. Weber, could I add to this, that to ask the witness seven times, Neretva river, is that Neretva a strategic goal, et cetera, or is it -- the Chamber has a -- I wouldn't say a thorough but at least a firm understanding of strategic goals, and unless there's any specific reason to -- what seems to be obvious in terms of language linked to strategic goals, that doesn't need that much further explanation. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, if you have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, of course, it includes that the objection was denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if you have any comments on this task that's being referred to with respect to Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is of interest is looking at the timing because this meeting takes place on 8th of November, and 11 days later we have the release of directive for further operations number 4, which discusses tasks in relation to the situation in the -- in the Podrinje and -- and the Drina valley in great detail, showing consistency with, for example, at -- Mr. Krajisnik says in relation to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please go to Directive 4. It is P1968. If we could go directly to page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like focus first your attention on section 2 of this directive. There is no need, as we've heard, for you to comment unnecessarily on individual strategic goals. But could you please read the section and just indicate whether or not this confirms what had been accomplished up till date?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that's what the document says. So, I mean, we see a continuity in the nature of the operations that are being conducted, in continuity including consistency with the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please go to the top of page 3 in the English and page 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this directive, what tasks from Directive 3, the previous one, had not been carried out at the time of Directive 4?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Mladic gives or lists four tasks and they can be found at top of English number 3 and B/C/S page number 5. And I think -- I mean, as Your Honours have said, the link with the specific strategic goals is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we go to the top of page 4 of the English and page 7 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the top of this page, we are looking at a continuation of a section from the previous, related to aims of operations. Could you please tell us whether -- you have any comments about the aims of the operations ordered pursuant to Directive 4?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I mean, I'm sorry, I will probably repeat myself, that I see a consistency. When you look at all the directives, obviously they are released in different conditions, I mean, in relation to the gains the VRS has made while implementing the previous directive, the attitude of the international community plays also a role obviously in relation to the -- the defining the forthcoming tasks for the VRS, but otherwise there is a consistency for all -- I'd say for sure the first eight directives with the six strategic goals. The ninth directive is in my view a special given that it's released after the international community has launched a major intervention against the Bosnian Serbs and also the Bosnian Serbs have suffered significant losses in western Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there are talks ongoing at the higher level, I mean, in Belgrade, involving President Milosevic for a negotiated end to the conflict. And I'm talking now about the October /November 1995 time-period. But prior to that, as I mentioned, there is consistency between the directives, successive directives, and the six strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could focus you on one particular passage in this section. It's in the -- where General Mladic talks about the second stage. He states: [As read] "That -- that second stage is lasting until the final liberation of all -- the territories of RS." Could you please tell us how this relates to the long-term nature of directives that he issued?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the overall goal for the Bosnian Serbs is to establish a, quote/unquote, Serb republic that includes all the territories that, in view of the -- or in the opinion of the Bosnian Serbs are Serb. The problem as I mentioned during the previous days is that at least in the beginning of the war that also includes territories where the Serbs do not have a majority, and, I mean, in those territories where they also have a majority, there are still non-Serbs present who do not necessarily want to stay in a, quote/unquote, Serbian republic but who prefer to stay in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 5 of the English and page 11 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is in the tasks section of the directive, under, I believe, part (d) is the tasks for the Drina Corps. Do you have any comments on these tasks that were issued to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to what I mentioned earlier to the comments by Mr. Krajisnik at the meeting in Bijeljina on the 8th of November, where he spoke about the need to remove the Muslim population from the -- the wider Drina valley. And -- and, here under the tasks of the Drina Corps, this -- those comments are explicitly included.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P2095.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 24 November 1992 decision for further operations from Zivanovic. Does this document from Zivanovic indicate that Directive 4 was immediately implemented by the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, this order by the commander of the Drina Corps is consistent with the tasks he has received from General Mladic through directive for further operations, number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you have any other comments on what Zivanovic orders under item 1?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, obviously the order of the corps is more detailed than the -- than the directive. Because the lower you go in the hierarchy, the more specific instruction -- sorry, orders will become. And this is consistent with doctrine. But, again, the commander's intent, as was expressed in the Directive number 4, is reflected in -- in this order by the Drina Corps, and the references to the Muslim population are -- again, as I mentioned, consistent with the instructions received through Directive number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your report you analyse a number of VRS operations. I'm not going to go through all of them with you today. But among them are Operation Udar, Proboj, Proljece, Mac 1, 2, and 3. Were these operations carried out, in part, by the Drina Corps between January and June 1993?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were they carried out in a manner consistent with the -- with Directive 4?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and that also applies to similar operations conducted in 1994, because there was, for example, Mac 94, as you can see on English page 169 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 05500.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I was still trying to find in the previous document, which was the Drina Corps order to the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade, whether it was also specifically mentioned that the civilian population should leave with the -- but I may have missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm happy to return to it if you're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Theunens tells us where I can find it, then -- it was still in paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on the top half of the page -- of the English page -- I mean, of page 1 in English on the top half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 1. I'll further look at it, and if I still can't find it later, then I'll come back to it. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I mean, it was on the top of the page we saw at the end, so I think that was page 2, where it was stated to remove the Muslim population from Cerska, Zepa, and Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll find, or not, and, if not, then I'll let you know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a 2 May 1993 combat order from Drina Corps Deputy Commander Skocajic. Could you please tell us what the status of the operations are according to the first paragraph of this report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, by that date the United Nations have declared the Srebrenica enclave a safe area. And the VRS Main Staff, I mean, in the introduction to the order when they provide an overview of the general situation addresses that decision by describing it as, quote/unquote, internationalising the problem of the area of Podrinje. Yeah, reference also made to the agreement on the demilitarisation of Srebrenica. So that's basically the operational context in which -- in which this order has to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the -- page 3 of the English, and the bottom of page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I'm referring you to section 2 of this order, setting out the task of the army. Do you have any observations on this section.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on the expression "ocisti" or "clearing up." I understand that sometimes there's confusion because it's translated as cleansing and then associations are made with ethnic cleansing. But from a military point of view, clearing the battle-field means to remove resistance pockets or pockets of enemy forces that may still be present as well as unexploded explosive, corpses of -- of, I mean, animals or anything else that is left that may interfere with the control one has over the territory that one has captured. So it's a normal tactical concept. And otherwise, there is again a reference to enabling -- I mean, in the fourth line of paragraph 2: [As read] "Enable the Muslim population to move out to other areas, the central part of the former BH, or to recognise the authority of the RS." And I think have addressed that earlier, that is, that -- I mean, strategic goal number 1, it is not excluded that non-Serbs who are loyal, as it is described, to the RS or who accept Serbian rule, quote/unquote, as it is sometimes mentioned in VRS documents, those people can stay but the others, as is illustrated here, have to -- to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 5500 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives P3070, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3070 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 13437.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a VRS Main Staff report on the conclusions from the assessment of the situation. Did you review this document during proofing? Dated 30 May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the second paragraph, under the strategic and operational -- operative situation and problems, how does this paragraph relate to the exercise of command and control by the Main Staff during the operations that were carried out in the Podrinje area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in relation to the -- to the -- the -- the role of the Main Staff, it is explicitly mentioned that representatives of the Main Staff of the VRS have been in the zone of operations of the Drina Corps since January 1993, and there also -- a forward command post has been established in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the following paragraph, is there a direct reference to strategic objective number 3?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is, Your Honours. I mean, between the quotation marks at the end of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Going onto the next paragraph, what does -- do you have any comments on what that shows in terms of the Muslim forces and others?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it shows that actually three enclaves have been created as a result of operations, so part of the population -- or the majority, actually, of the Muslim population has -- has fled according to the document, and the reminder -- remainder, sorry, of the troops of the ABiH are grouped in three enclaves: Srebrenica, Zepa, and Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm noting the time. This is a -- a good spot to -- to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to address the Prosecution on two exhibits. On the -- this is about the decision on the 38th Rule 92 bis motion. On the 28th of November, the Chamber has admitted into evidence two maps of Rogatica; namely, P3019 and P3026. Both maps have B/C/S writings on them, and there are no English translations attached. The Prosecution is instructed to upload such translations and the Registry is already instructed to attach those translations once uploaded, unless the Prosecution would make a clear statement that it would not rely on any of those portions of text, but then we'd like to have that clearly on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the last document 65 ter 13437.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you please slowly repeat the number again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 13437.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The Defence has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Registrar is invited to assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives number P3071, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3071 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 23609.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is a VRS Main Staff security intelligence report regarding the percentage of territory held by each of the three ethnic groups in BH. The report is from Colonel Tolimir and is dated 14 September 1993. What does this report show?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the report shows the Bosnian Serb interpretation of the situation on the battle-field, i.e., what amount of territory is controlled by which party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And with respect to the VRS, how much territory is controlled?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the document, 68.09 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And does this also then describe the territory controlled by what is the so-called BiH army?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please scroll down in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does and this -- I mean, this so-called BH army stands for the ABiH. And then a distinction is made with Cazin Krajina because by that time or maybe a bit later because I -- is the document from September 1993? It is difficult to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was. It was dated 14 September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Then Fikret Abdic declares his own entity, the so-called Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia, in the northern part of the Cazin Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have the next page English. I believe the information is still on this page in the B/C/S. Do you have any comments on the enclaves that are indicated on this page?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it -- I mean, the document shows the -- the three -- it shows Sarajevo as an enclave and then the three enclaves in eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 23609.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number P3072, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P359, page 53 of both versions. And, Your Honours, when this comes up, if it would expedite the record, I would be happy to lead in the attendees at this meeting if it's not objected to by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed as suggested, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, coming up before you will be another entry from General Mladic's notebooks regarding a meeting on the 13th and 14th of December, 1993. In attendance from Serbia are Slobodan Milosevic, General Perisic, Zoran Sokolovic, the head of the Serbian MUP; Jovica Stanisic, the assistant minister of the Serbian MUP and chief of the State Security Service; Radovan Stojicic aka Badza, an assistant minister of the Serbian MUP, head of public security; Milan Tepavcevic, a deputy of Mr. Stanisic, Jovica [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And General Mrksic. The names that -- from the RS had been discussed many times on the record. Did you review this meeting during proofing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reviewed these notes during proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you have any comments on Jovica Stanisic's initial statement and what the purpose of this meeting is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to the -- the -- the -- the comments attributed to Jovica Stanisic, the meeting is about Serbia assisting the Bosnian Serbs in order to improve their, quote/unquote, operational and tactical position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now, on Tuesday, at page 20264, I asked you at what level of command are strategic decisions made, and you provided an answer about the various levels of decision-making at the strategic level, operational level, and tactical level. Do you have any comments on this page based on what level of either planning or decision-making is involved at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
